narrative.overview:
Everything this product makes ends up printed: on a menu, a table tent, a shop window, a business card. The interface is the proof sheet that comes before the print run. A proof is trusted because it is exact: it shows precisely what will be printed, its size and format, and it never shows something that will not come out right. That is the standard every screen is held to.

The voice is assured and professional. Calm warm paper instead of cold grey, deep ink for text, one signal color for action and readiness, precise numbers in a monospaced spec line. Controls are the standard ones of the web, drawn firmly: clear borders, generous touch targets, unmistakable states. Personality lives in exact details, never in decoration: the crop marks around the preview, the spec line under it, a themed caret and text selection. The visual world rejects the free-tool category look outright: no ad banners, pop-ups, blinking upgrade buttons or fake countdowns, and no decorative purple gradients, glassmorphism or neon glow.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, deep ink text, one signal teal for action and state.
Standard web controls, firm borders (3:1 or better), 44 px touch targets on phones.
Flat surfaces separated by rules and tone; shadows only for what floats above content.
A proof frame with crop marks whose color carries the state of what it holds.
Exact measurements in a monospaced, tabular spec voice.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Teal is the only accent. It marks the primary action of an area and state, never decoration; there is at most one teal button in view per area.

rules.name: The Two Edges Rule
rules.body: Rule color outlines structure; Control Edge outlines what responds to input. A border that looks interactive must be interactive.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: The QR code always sits on white, in both themes. A proof is never shown on a dark tile.

rules.name: The Measured Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace appears only for values that are measured or exact (sizes, colors, codes). Never for headings, labels or decoration.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: Sizes are fixed rem steps (ratio about 1.2); no fluid clamp() type in the product.

rules.name: The Float-Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this sits above the page". Panels, tiles, inputs and buttons never carry one.

dos: Do keep Signal Teal for the primary action and for state; one teal button per area.
Do outline every control with Control Edge (`#78716c` / `#8a837c`) and every structure with Rule.
Do make touch targets at least 44px tall on phones.
Do set measured values (sizes, hex colors, codes) in Geist Mono with tabular numerals.
Do show the QR code on white in both themes, framed by crop marks that tell its state.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces: text selection, caret, focus ring, `accent-color`.
Do keep transitions between 150 and 250ms and for state changes only; respect reduced motion.
donts: Don't use the free-tool category look: no ad banners, pop-ups, blinking "Upgrade" buttons or fake countdowns.
Don't use decorative purple gradients, glassmorphism or neon glow. The one blur in the system is the phone bar's backdrop, there for legibility over scrolling content.
Don't put shadows on panels, tiles, inputs or buttons; shadows are for floating layers only.
Don't show a QR code that cannot be printed or scanned, even dimmed.
Don't use monospace for headings, labels or as a "technical" costume.
Don't add a second accent color or tint surfaces other than the selected tile.
